subject: Failover activation lead time & RTO/RPO amendment request (FinSecure)
messages:
From: Daniel Park <dpark@finsecure.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@finsecure.com
Date: 2026-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Activation lead time / RTO & RPO carveout request

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We’re reviewing Redwood’s standard DR commitments and have a specific constraint for APAC failover due to a set of on-prem connectors at our processing edge. Those connectors require manual reconfiguration and a state reconciliation step that realistically prevents sub-30-minute activation.

Request: would Redwood consider a contractual carveout for our account that permits an activation window of up to 2 hours for APAC failover events, with an RTO of 2 hours and an RPO up to 15 minutes, limited to the three services listed in the attached architecture diagram?

We understand this is outside your standard SLA. We’re open to compensating via reserved capacity commitment or an operational readiness program. We attached an architecture diagram and a short runbook we use internally to show the constraint.

Can we get a brief written position so our procurement team can decide next steps?

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Ops, FinSecure
dpark@finsecure.com
+65 9123 4567

Attachment: finsecure-arch-diagram.pdf
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation lead time / RTO & RPO carveout request

Hi Daniel —

Appreciate the clear summary and the diagram — that helps a lot. Short answer: we can discuss a bounded carveout, but we need to align on scope, risk mitigations, and operational controls before committing.

A few immediate notes:
- We can offer conditional carveouts limited to particular service IDs and geographic regions rather than account-wide exceptions.
- Options to reduce your activation time: warm-standby with pre-warmed containers, a lightweight state reconciliation helper we can supply, or a hybrid approach where critical streams use async replication to keep RPO near-zero.
- Tradeoffs: expanded carveouts typically require a reserved-capacity commitment or a higher tier on our Dedicated offering to ensure isolation during warm-up.

Marissa (CS lead) and Logan (infra) are copied to assess operational impacts and to draft a runbook + acceptance criteria. Can we schedule a 30-minute call Tuesday to walk through the diagram and identify which services qualify for exception?

I’ll pull together a draft amendment and a suggested 90-day pilot cadence so procurement has tangible terms.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-11T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation lead time / RTO & RPO carveout request

Priya / Logan —

I reviewed FinSecure’s diagram. Quick internal read: granting a 2-hour activation RTO for a subset of services is feasible if we codify the scope and enforce tight operational controls. Suggested mitigations to include in the amendment:

1) Scoped carveout list: explicitly enumerate service IDs and endpoints that are permitted the extended activation window.
2) Pre-approved runbook: both parties sign a joint runbook; activation is only valid if runbook checklist is followed. I attached a runbook-stub for internal use.
3) Timebox: 6-month pilot period with telemetry gates (error rates, failover time observed) before we consider long-term changes.
4) Capacity/financial offset: require a minimum 12-month reserved capacity commitment (Dedicated) or a quarterly operational readiness fee to offset extra on-call/resourcing during warmups.

I recommend we position this as a conditional pilot with an opt-out clause. If accepted, CS will own the canary schedule and post-mortem gating criteria.

Attachment: runbook-stub.md

-Marissa
Director, Customer Success
marissa_cole@redwood.com
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-12T14:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation lead time / RTO & RPO carveout request — technical notes

Team —

Technical analysis notes for the amendment draft:

- Warm-up timeline: with pre-warmed containers + cached artifacts, node initialization is ~20–30 minutes; the long pole is state reconciliation for the edge connectors and DB schema migrations. Practically, we should budget ~90–120 minutes for full functional parity in APAC when those connectors require manual steps.

- RPO options:
  * For critical streams, we can offer near-zero RPO via a lightweight async replication overlay. That will require a small dedicated replication pool and additional egress throughput (estimate +5–8% on committed capacity).
  * For non-critical services, 15-minute RPO can be met using our existing prefix/KV caching if the connector supports resume tokens.

- Operational controls to include in amendment: pre-failover smoke tests, mandatory telemetry forwarding to Redwood for 72 hours post-activation, and a single dedicated on-call handover for the first 30 days of any pilot activation.

I’ll provide a concise ops checklist for the legal/contract team to reference. If procurement accepts reserved capacity, add a clause that gives us 72-hour notice before a planned switchover to pre-warm nodes.

-Logan
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
logan_wright@redwood.com
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@finsecure.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T16:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Activation lead time / RTO & RPO carveout request — proposal and next steps

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for your patience while we scoped this internally. To summarize a concrete path forward we can share with procurement:

Proposal (conditional pilot):
- Scope: carveout limited to the three service IDs in your diagram.
- Term: 6-month pilot starting after canary validation.
- Activation commitments: Redwood will accept an up-to-2-hour activation window for the scoped services, with an RTO of 2 hours and an RPO up to 15 minutes for non-critical streams. For streams designated as critical by FinSecure, we can provide an add-on async replication overlay to achieve near-zero RPO (additional capacity charge applies).
- Controls: joint signed runbook required, mandatory smoke-tests, telemetry export for 72 hours post-activation, and a post-activation post-mortem within 7 days.
- Commercials: require either a 12-month Dedicated reserved capacity commitment or a quarterly operational readiness fee to cover standby resources.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm with procurement whether you prefer the reserved capacity option or operational readiness fees.
2) Sign-off on the runbook (I attached a draft).
3) We propose a canary failover on 2026-06-01 (off-hours) to validate timelines — Redwood will provide a test plan and on-call support.

If you’re comfortable, we can issue a DocuSign amendment for the pilot and a HubSpot note with the proposed commercial term. Link to DocuSign draft: https://docusign.example.com/seq/AX1234. HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deals/FS-2026-0897.

If that all sounds reasonable, confirm here and we’ll move the amendment through legal.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com
